title: Theo and the Veil
premise: Astrid Pemberton has spent her life in the Veiled Valley, the one place where magic cannot reach, safe from the usurper Veylan whose armies now swallow the free cities. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than kingdoms, Astrid learns the child carries the stolen soul of her guild's last true mage — sold to the court beneath the mountain in exchange for the valley's protection. Descending into the deep court with the child and a disgraced royal cartographer she comes to love, Astrid must bargain with, betray, and finally defy the thing that bought her people's safety. She reclaims the soul at the cost of her own memories of the valley, returning to lead the dying guild — changed, half-remembering, but free.
about_author: Cyrus Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about institutions, inheritance, and the quiet violence of bargains struck on other people's behalf.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet the Veiled Valley and its dwindling guild through a routine ritual day: mending wards that no longer hum, tending an aging master who barely remembers her name. The emotional beat is quiet dread — Astrid loves this place and suspects it is already dead. It ends when a knock sounds at the gate at dusk.

chapters.title: A Child Speaking Rain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A mud-caked girl of six appears at the door, uttering syllables no living tongue should know; the valley's oldest ward-stone answers her, glowing for the first time in decades. The guild elders panic and vote to turn her out. Astrid defies them, taking the child in. Beat: stubborn compassion against institutional fear.

chapters.title: What the Elders Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating Astrid and Master Corwin's POV. Deciphering the child's speech reveals the guild's founding sin: their founder sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy the valley's magic-free sanctuary. The child is not random — she is the vessel carrying that soul home. Beat: horror at inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Introduce Tam Voss, POV his. A disgraced royal mapmaker caught sketching the valley's approaches is dragged before the guild. He offers passage through the usurper's lines in exchange for asylum, confessing he once mapped the deep court itself. Astrid argues to trust him. Beat: wary attraction kindled over shared maps and lies.

chapters.title: Leaving the Veil
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The three slip out through the mountain pass as Veylan's outriders burn the lowland farms. Outside the veil, magic floods back into the world — and into Astrid, revealing a talent the valley had suppressed. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear as she realizes power always wants more.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Crossing occupied territory, they shelter with resistance cells Tam once betrayed under torture. He must face the people he condemned; Astrid chooses to stand beside him anyway. The child begins speaking fragments of memory that are not hers — the founder's soul surfacing. Beat: love tested by shame.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They descend through a drowned cathedral into the deep court, where the soul-buyer — an ancient, patient entity wearing the founder's face — holds court among centuries of purchased souls. It offers Astrid anything she names. Beat: seduction of power; she nearly accepts before the child's hand anchors her.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Negotiation becomes trap: the entity demands a soul in trade, and Tam offers his own to save Astrid and the child. Astrid refuses to let him, and instead bargains away her memories of the valley — the one thing she cannot bear to lose. Beat: love against duty, both wounded.

chapters.title: Veylan at the Gates
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. As the usurper's army reaches the free cities, the reclaimed soul ignites; the child speaks whole again, and the founder's knowledge flows through Astrid. She turns the deep court's hoarded power outward, shattering Veylan's advance — and feels how easily it could corrupt her. Beat: triumph shadowed by temptation survived.

chapters.title: Half-Remembered Home
chapters.summary: Resolution, Astrid's POV. Astrid returns to the valley able to recall its shape but not its feeling, guided by Tam's maps and the child's hand in hers. The guild rebuilds around memory kept by others rather than held alone. Final beat: bittersweet peace — she gave up her past to buy everyone a future, and finds love can be a new kind of remembering.
